assertions.description: Iterator.zip is exposed as a function. Expected to FAIL before Chrome 153 (the surface is absent even behind flags on Chromium ≤141).
Iterator.zipKeyed is exposed as a function. Expected to FAIL before Chrome 153.
The default mode is "shortest": zip([[1,2,3],['a','b']]) yields exactly two positional pairs.
mode "longest" continues past exhausted inputs using the per-input padding value.
mode "strict" throws a TypeError when the inputs complete after different numbers of yields. Guarded on Iterator.zip existing so an absent API fails instead of false-passing via its own TypeError.
assertions.test: typeof Iterator !== 'undefined' && typeof Iterator.zip === 'function' && (() => { try { Iterator.zip([[1, 2, 3], ['a', 'b']], { mode: 'strict' }).toArray(); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: An unknown mode string throws a TypeError before any iteration starts. Guarded on Iterator.zip existing so an absent API fails instead of false-passing via its own TypeError.
assertions.test: typeof Iterator !== 'undefined' && typeof Iterator.zip === 'function' && (() => { try { Iterator.zip([[1]], { mode: 'zippy' }); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: A primitive (e.g. a string) inside the iterable of iterables is rejected with a TypeError — strings are not silently iterated as characters (GetIteratorFlattenable with reject-primitives). Guarded on Iterator.zip existing so an absent API fails instead of false-passing via its own TypeError.
assertions.test: typeof Iterator !== 'undefined' && typeof Iterator.zip === 'function' && (() => { try { Iterator.zip([[1, 2], 'ab']).toArray(); return false; } catch (e) { return e instanceof TypeError; } })()

assertions.description: Iterator.zipKeyed yields null-prototype objects keyed like the input object (OrdinaryObjectCreate(null) in the finishResults closure).
assertions.test: (() => { const row = Iterator.zipKeyed({ a: [1], b: ['x'] }).toArray()[0]; return Object.getPrototypeOf(row) === null && row.a === 1 && row.b === 'x'; })()

assertions.description: Calling return() on the zip helper (e.g. breaking a for…of) closes every underlying iterator — the generators' finally blocks run (IteratorCloseAll).
assertions.test: (() => { let closed = 0; function* g() { try { while (true) yield 1; } finally { closed++; } } const it = Iterator.zip([g(), g()]); it.next(); it.return(); return closed === 2; })()
